requirements.lead_text: Demonstrate that you know how to respond to electrical emergencies by doing the following:
requirements.req_text: Demonstrate that you know how to respond to electrical emergencies by doing the following: (a) Explain how to turn off power for a particular circuit and the whole house in the event of an emergency. (b) Demonstrate how to rescue a person touching a live wire in the home. (c) Describe how to safely get out of a car in an accident if you suspect a utility wire is on the car. (d) Show how to render first aid to a person who is unconscious from an apparent electrical shock. (e) Show how to treat an electrical burn. (f) Explain what to do in the event of an electrical fire. (g) Explain what to do if caught out in the open during an electrical storm.

pamphlet_excerpts: Electricity Sub-Req 10a: Connect a buzzer, bell, or light with a battery. Have a key or switch in the line.
Electricity Sub-Req 10b: Make and run a simple electric motor (from a kit is acceptable, if approved by your counselor ahead of time).
Electricity Sub-Req 10c: Build a simple rheostat. Show that it works.
Electricity Sub-Req 10d: Build a single-pole, double-throw switch. Show that it works.
step_by_step_procedure: Prepare & Inspect (Req 10): Review the official Electricity requirement standard and verify all required tools, reference tables, and safety gear.
Analyze Core Principles: Identify the primary concepts, definitions, and cause-and-effect relationships governing (a) Connect a buzzer, bell, or light with.
Execute & Document: Perform the explain task methodically with your patrol buddy and log specific observations in your Electricity Workbook.
Verify With Counselor: Present your completed work, demonstrate proficiency, and answer Socratic check-for-understanding questions for Blue Card sign-off.

Discuss what you learned with your counselor and whether you might be interested in this career.
